open_points.subject: credential echo handling for file responses
open_points.text: “A service's own answer body that echoes one verbatim is withheld from everyone” contradicts “one that carries it … inside a file the kernel only moves, cannot be recognised”; A09 rule 7 also says “Every body as read, whatever its status … is searched … for the bytes of the credential value”.
open_points.question: Must service_invoker search a response body for the credential when that body is a declared file output, or are file bodies exempt from credential-echo detection?
options: Search every response body, including file outputs, and withhold a matching file
Do not inspect declared file-output bodies for credential echoes; protect them only by disclosure class
open_points.default_guess: Search every response body, including file outputs, because A09 gives the explicit operational rule.

open_points.subject: personal-data promise for agents with direct service access
open_points.text: “An agent's own access to a service … is granted by that service and the owner outside the kernel; … its personal-data promise (K-14) covers what the kernel itself returns” conflicts with “Personal data … reach an agent only as digest and class; the owner alone reads them” and A07's “no agent ever holds it.”
open_points.question: Is the prohibition on an agent receiving personal-data content limited to kernel responses, or is it intended to constrain the agent's independently granted direct access to microservices too?
options: Limit K-14 and A07 disclosure enforcement to values returned by the kernel surface
Require direct microservice access also to prevent agents receiving personal-data content
open_points.default_guess: Limit the promise to the kernel surface, because the changed exclusion explicitly places direct service access outside kernel authority.
